title: Shell.prism(): every side face of every shell prism is inside-out (outward-normal test inverted)
evidence: `if area > 0.0: nrm = -nrm` flips (d.y, 0, -d.x), which already is the outward normal of a counter-clockwise polygon. Unit probe: a unit prism built from CCW points and from CW points both gave 8 of 8 side triangles whose stored normal points INTO the prism. In the built ship the room-facing face of the north wall of `core` (z = -12.85) stored n = (0,0,-1). Shell.tri() derives the winding from the normal, so the room-facing faces were back-face culled and all walls, baseboards, window frames, glass and cladding were drawn by their FAR faces: walls 15 cm behind their colliders, frames/reveals inside-out (compare tour 01_bridge before/after: the white 'ghost pillars' around the windows are gone), every coplanar analysis ran on the wrong faces.
impact: Walls, trims, frames and plating rendered 3-15 cm away from where they collide, window reveals inside-out, lighting normals of the visible faces reversed relative to the geometry; hid the real z-fights listed below (G023..G035).
fix: Flip the normal only for clockwise polygons (`area < 0.0`).
resolution: Re-verified on the 5-deck tree: a unit prism from CCW points had 8 of 8 side triangles with the normal pointing into the prism. Fixed in ship_builder.gd Shell.prism. | hunter: ship_builder.gd Shell.prism fixed. Kept fixed by godot/tests/round2_test.gd::_test_prism_normals (both windings + the core wall face) and by zfight_test, which now analyses the correct faces.

title: All 56 PBR surface / screen / sky PNGs are imported WITHOUT mipmaps: floors, walls, ceiling tiles and the sky shimmer and crawl while walking
evidence: `godot --import` writes `mipmaps/generate=false` (the editor's 'detect 3D' never runs headless): 56 of 56 textures/*.png.import files (33 of them the surface maps used by ShipMaterials.surface) had it off. Probe: `load('res://textures/surfaces/hull_panel_albedo.png').get_image().has_mipmaps()` == false for hull_panel_albedo, deck_plate_normal, ceiling_orm, screens/alert, sky/stars, sky/planet. The materials ask for LINEAR_WITH_MIPMAPS_ANISOTROPIC, but there is no mip chain to filter with, so a 512 px texture tiled every 4 m is point-minified (about 6 texels per pixel at 20 m) and sparkles with every camera movement. Measured with the new godot/tests/flicker_check.gd (7 cameras, shader time frozen, mean |dL| between frames 1 mm apart; ALL round-2 fixes together, mipmaps being the dominant texture term): original -> fixed ship 01_bridge 0.00176 -> 0.00129, 02_corF1 0.00153 -> 0.00118, 12_hydro 0.00232 -> 0.00220, 14_armory 0.00339 -> 0.00324, 19_life 0.00242 -> 0.00210, 22_hangar 0.00137 -> 0.00114, 23_towerA2 0.00350 -> 0.00268 (-4 .. -27 %); pixels flickering > 6 % luma: tower 1.065 % -> 0.825 %, armory 0.889 % -> 0.844 %.
impact: The 'lot of textures that are flickering' the user reports: every textured surface of the ship at a distance.
fix: project.godot [importer_defaults] texture mipmaps/generate=true for new imports, plus a load-time repair for stale imports: scripts/texture_fix.gd (TextureFix.fix_tree) reads each texture's .import file and, only if mipmaps are off, swaps in an ImageTexture with a generated mip chain (cached per file).
resolution: Re-verified: project.godot already had texture mipmaps/generate=true (importer default), but that only affects NEW imports. Ported scripts/texture_fix.gd (TextureFix.fix_tree, called at the end of ShipBuilder.build) as the load-time repair for stale .import files. | hunter: project.godot + godot/scripts/texture_fix.gd + ShipBuilder.build() calls TextureFix.fix_tree(self). Kept fixed by godot/tests/round2_test.gd::_test_textures (every surface kind has mips, forced TextureFix conversion yields a mipmapped ImageTexture, the import file itself says mipmaps on). Existing checkouts: delete the untracked *.png.import files and re-run godot --import (the runtime repair covers them meanwhile).

title: Deck-map stair labels are inverted on the end decks and hard-wired to 3 decks
evidence: `up := deck > 1; dn := deck < 3; t = 'UP/DN' if up and dn else ('UP' if dn else 'DN')`. Deck 1 is the TOP deck (y 8.0): up = false, dn = true -> label 'UP' although the stairs only lead down; deck 3 (bottom) gets 'DN'. `3` is a literal, so a 4- or 5-deck ship labels every middle deck wrongly.

fix: DeckMap.stair_hint(decks, deck) compares deck heights: UP if a deck lies higher, DN if one lies lower.

title: Ambient hum / engine rumble loops are cut at 3.2 s of an 8 s clip (QOA-compressed WAVs)
evidence: The importer's default `compress/mode=2` (QOA) makes AudioStreamWAV.format == 3. `_loop()` only knows 16/8-bit and set loop_end = data.size() / 1 = 71408 'frames' (3.24 s at 22050 Hz) for a clip of 176400 frames (8.0 s). Probe: ambient_hum.wav fmt=3 bytes=71408 len=8.0.
impact: The loop restarts in the middle of the waveform every 3.2 s (audible click / pulsing hum).
fix: MainScript.loop_frames() = length x mix_rate, independent of the storage format; project.godot [importer_defaults] wav compress/mode=0 (PCM16) so the loops are not compressed.
resolution: Re-verified: the loop length is now loop_frames() (length x mix_rate); project.godot [importer_defaults] wav compress/mode=0. NOTE: .import files are git-ignored, so a stale local cache keeps QOA until godot/audio/*.wav.import is deleted and `godot --import` is re-run; round2_test::_test_audio_loops reports this. | hunter: main.gd + project.godot. evidence: Colliders are the only occluders; the cladding has none, so slab end faces covered by cladding (e.g. `Mesh_ceiling | Mesh_floor 4.0 m2 at (13.0, 7.77, -2.22)`, `Mesh_ceiling | Mesh_clad`) were reported as visible.
impact: False positives that hide real findings.
fix: ShipBuilder.clad_hulls (convex hulls of the plating pieces) become a temporary occluder layer in the test.
resolution: ship_builder.gd + zfight_test.gd.
